questions.text: Compare OSI 7-Layer Reference Model vs TCP/IP Protocol Suite. Explain functions, protocols, addressing schemes, and data units (PDUs) at each layer with block diagrams.
Explain Network Topologies: Star, Ring, Mesh, Bus, Tree, and Hybrid topologies. Compare them based on cable cost, fault tolerance, scalability, and ease of troubleshooting.
Explain Switching Techniques: Circuit Switching, Packet Switching (Datagram vs Virtual Circuit approaches), and Message Switching. Compare delay, throughput, and resource allocation.

Explain Guided Transmission Media: Twisted Pair (UTP Cat 5/6, STP), Coaxial Cable (Thinnet vs Thicknet), and Optical Fiber (Single-Mode vs Multi-Mode Step/Graded Index). Explain total internal reflection and attenuation.

Explain Theoretical Maximum Data Rate Limits: Nyquist Bit Rate formula ($C = 2B \log_2 M$) for noiseless channels and Shannon Capacity Theorem ($C = B \log_2(1 + SNR)$) for noisy channels. Calculate channel capacity for a $3\text{ kHz}$ telephone line with $SNR = 30\text{ dB}$.
Explain Multiplexing Techniques: Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM), Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM), and Time Division Multiplexing (Synchronous TDM vs Statistical/Asynchronous TDM).

Explain Data Link Layer Design Issues: Services provided to network layer, Framing methods (Character count, Byte stuffing with escape chars, Bit stuffing with `01111110` flag). Stuff bits into: `0110111111011111001`.

Explain Error Detection Codes: Parity Check, Checksum, and Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC). Given data $1101011011$ and generator polynomial $G(x) = x^4 + x + 1$, compute transmitted CRC frame and verify error detection at receiver.
Explain Error Correction: Hamming (7, 4) Code. Calculate parity bits for 4-bit data `1011` and show single-bit error detection and correction at receiver.

Explain Flow Control Protocols: Stop-and-Wait ARQ, Go-Back-N (GBN) ARQ, and Selective Repeat (SR) ARQ. Derive channel efficiency formula $\eta = \frac{N}{1 + 2a}$ where $a = \frac{T_{prop}}{T_{trans}}$. Explain why sender window size in SR must be $\le 2^{m-1}$.

Explain Medium Access Control (MAC) Random Access Protocols: Pure ALOHA and Slotted ALOHA. Derive maximum throughput $S_{\max} = \frac{1}{2e} \approx 18.4\%$ for Pure ALOHA and $S_{\max} = \frac{1}{e} \approx 36.8\%$ for Slotted ALOHA.

Explain Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) protocols: 1-Persistent, Non-Persistent, and p-Persistent CSMA. Explain CSMA/CD (Collision Detection) used in Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) and derive minimum frame size condition $L_{\min} \ge 2 \times T_{prop} \times \text{Bandwidth}$. Explain Binary Exponential Backoff algorithm.

Explain CSMA/CA (Collision Avoidance) used in Wireless LAN (IEEE 802.11 WiFi). Explain Hidden Terminal and Exposed Terminal problems and how RTS/CTS (Request to Send / Clear to Send) handshake and NAV (Network Allocation Vector) solve them.
Explain Ethernet Standards: Fast Ethernet (100Base-TX, 100Base-FX), Gigabit Ethernet (1000Base-T, 1000Base-SX/LX) and 10-Gigabit Ethernet. Explain Ethernet MAC frame format.

Explain IPv4 Addressing Architecture: Classful Addressing (Classes A, B, C, D, E) and Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR). Explain Subnet Masking, Default Gateway, and Network / Broadcast addresses.

VLSM Subnetting Problem: An organization is assigned the network block `192.168.1.0/24`. The organization has 4 departments requiring 55, 26, 12, and 6 host IP addresses respectively. Design an optimal VLSM subnet scheme specifying Subnet ID, Subnet Mask, Usable IP Range, and Directed Broadcast Address for each department.

Explain IPv4 Datagram Header format and describe all fields: Version, IHL, Type of Service (ToS), Total Length, Identification, Flags ($DF, MF$), Fragment Offset, Time to Live (TTL), Protocol, Header Checksum, Source & Destination IP.

Explain IPv4 Packet Fragmentation: An IPv4 datagram of $4000\text{ bytes}$ (including $20\text{ bytes}$ IP header) arrives at a router that must forward it over a link with $MTU = 1500\text{ bytes}$. Calculate the number of fragments, Total Length, Flags ($DF, MF$), and Fragment Offset values for each fragment.
Explain IPv6: Features, 128-bit address representation, IPv6 Base Header (Fixed 40 bytes), Extension Headers, and Transition Strategies from IPv4 to IPv6 (Dual Stack, Tunneling, Header Translation).
Explain Distance Vector Routing (DVR) algorithm based on Bellman-Ford equation. Explain the Count-to-Infinity problem and its solutions: Split Horizon and Poison Reverse.
Explain Link State Routing (LSR) algorithm. Explain Link State Packets (LSP), Flooding, and Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm. Compare DVR vs LSR.
Explain Routing Protocols: Intra-domain routing (RIP vs OSPF) vs Inter-domain routing (BGP - Border Gateway Protocol path vector routing).

Explain Address Resolution Protocol (ARP), Reverse ARP (RARP), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP DORA mechanism: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge), and Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP error and query messages).
Explain Network Address Translation (NAT) and Port Address Translation (NAPT / PAT). Explain Private IP address ranges (RFC 1918) and translation table mapping.
Explain Transport Layer Services: Process-to-Process Delivery, Port Numbers (Well-known, Registered, Dynamic/Private ports), Sockets, Multiplexing and Demultiplexing. Compare TCP vs UDP.
Explain TCP Segment Header format: Sequence Number, Acknowledgement Number, Data Offset, Flags ($URG, ACK, PSH, RST, SYN, FIN$), Window Size, Checksum, and Urgent Pointer.
Explain TCP Connection Management: 3-Way Handshake Connection Establishment ($SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK$) and 4-Way Handshake Connection Termination with state transition diagrams.

Explain TCP Congestion Control Algorithms: Slow Start ($CWND$ doubles exponentially), Congestion Avoidance ($AIMD$ linear increase), Fast Retransmit (3 duplicate ACKs), and Fast Recovery with Congestion Window ($CWND$) vs Time graph.

Explain TCP Flow Control (Sliding Window and Silly Window Syndrome with Nagle's algorithm and Clark's solution) and TCP Retransmission Timer Calculation (Jacobson's / Karn's algorithm for RTT estimation).
Explain Domain Name System (DNS): Hierarchical namespace (Root, TLD, Authoritative DNS), DNS Records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR), and Iterative vs Recursive DNS Query resolution with diagram.

Explain Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP): HTTP Request/Response format, HTTP Methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD), Persistent vs Non-Persistent HTTP, Cookies, Caching, and HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP).
Explain Electronic Mail (E-Mail) Architecture: User Agent (UA), Message Transfer Agent (MTA), Message Access Agent (MAA). Explain SMTP, POP3, IMAP, and MIME format.

Explain Cryptography: Symmetric Key (Symmetric Ciphers: AES, DES) vs Asymmetric Public Key Cryptography (RSA). RSA Problem: Given prime numbers $p = 7, q = 11$, and public encryption key $e = 13$, determine private key $d$ and encrypt message $M = 9$.
Explain Digital Signatures, Cryptographic Hash Functions (SHA-256, MD5), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and SSL/TLS Handshake protocol for HTTPS security.
Explain Firewalls: Packet Filtering Firewall, Stateful Inspection Firewall, Application Gateway (Proxy Firewall), and Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS / IPS).
